policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'under him,' which is compatible with both the qere and ketiv forms; both accompanying notes are alternative_rendering notes and therefore do not decide the textual reading. Retain the documented qere base fallback.

ASV's main text reads 'with snow water,' matching qere בְמֵי ('with waters of'); the mapped textual_variant note, 'Another reading is, with snow,' identifies the ketiv alternative and confirms that the main ASV text selects r00-base.
